knowledge_point.title: Identifying Multiplicity of a Root Given a Graph

question.:question/problem:
![](images/33/33bec46293f976bfb829e987cd3ce26fa5cc67310bc830fc8f46b7f0d57b3acf.png)

A part of the graph of a polynomial $p(x)$ is given above. Which of the following statements is true?
question.:question/worked-solution:
| Multiplicity | Sketch | Sketch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ 

 (Simple Root) | ![](images/5a/5a0221f93c65a1eeb4503604a558a6da81c4c7af81c2c52cc35ecf3d189fe99f.png) | ![](images/d5/d556b4edf39181eebb7ec87c344d6f657a6875ecd2745405eaf5351ccaff6f96.png) |
| $>1$ 

 (Multiple Root) 

 Even | ![](images/9d/9d14c2588da2ee9c9f5bbc32a70791146bed609ea0d6d5912aeaa2edab02e2d7.png) | ![](images/28/28ad9248a9a509e3a44937d0438fb2366f550a22360d01b9b6a29bcac41357e8.png) |
| $>1$ 

 (Multiple Root) 

 Odd | ![](images/3a/3ae81378cb3c918dd5b7730519eb5a91e949f88eef9f03f4910f4ab8fb3cd5a9.png) | ![](images/95/9506a7ce4031f1f6244c0110c3235f66ea5652bb53548a032732869cf21f5997.png) |

It's possible to determine information regarding the multiplicities of the roots of a polynomial from its graph.

- If the graph intersects the $x$-axis but is *not* tangent to the $x$-axis at $x=a,$ we have a *simple* root $x=a.$

- If the graph is *tangent* to the $x$-axis at $x=a,$ we have a *multiple* root $x=a.$ Furthermore:

- If the graph touches the $x$-axis and reverses direction at $x=a,$ the multiplicity of a root $x=a$ is *even*.

- If the graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=a,$ the multiplicity of a root $x=a$ is *odd*.

In our case, the graph is *tangent* to the $x$-axis at $x=-1.$ So, $x=-1$ is a *multiple* root. 

Furthermore, the graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-1.$ So, $x=-1$ has *odd* multiplicity.

Therefore, $x=-1$ is a multiple root of odd multiplicity.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: $x=-1$ is a multiple root of even multiplicity
$x=-1$ is a multiple root of odd multiplicity
$x=-1$ is a simple root
$x=-1$ is a simple root of even multiplicity
$x=-1$ is not a root of $p(x)$
